title: Why you freeze mid-sentence (and 5 ways to say help) | Words That Stick #4
description:
You didn't forget the word. You're just not sure it fits. Too formal? Too rude? Too dramatic?

So learn one more thing with every word: its setting, and when to avoid it.
• swamped: fine at work. Avoid it when you only have one or two small tasks.
• livid: very angry. Avoid it when someone is just slightly annoyed.
• let me look into that: perfect for emails and meetings. Avoid it when you're chatting with friends.

5 ways to say "help", from casual to formal, one picture each:
• give me a hand: friends moving a sofa (casual)
• help: a neighbour carrying your heavy shopping (fine anywhere)
• support: the IT team fixing your laptop (common at work)
• assist: a hotel receptionist, "How may I assist you?" (formal; with friends it sounds stiff)
• aid: lorries bringing food after a flood (formal; you hear it on the news, not in everyday chat)

The rule: learn the setting, not just the meaning.

Try it tomorrow: next to each new word, write where it fits (friends, work, or both).

More words for "help": https://anotherwordfor.net/another-word-for-help/

Next episode: the 15-minute routine.
